course.programmeTitle: Bachelor of Engineering in Data Science and Engineering
course.title: Project Practicum II: Data Analytics & Machine Learning
course.description: Project Practicum 2 is a hands-on, project-based course designed to bridge the gap between theoretical machine learning knowledge and practical industry application. This course introduces core concepts related to artificial intelligence (AI), and the services in Microsoft Azure that can be used to create AI solutions.

clos.description: Understand and analyze core technologies and their practical applications.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Use "Design Thinking" sessions to map business needs to machine learning models, LLM and/or AI model.
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Problem Mapping: Identifies clear pain points. Model Selection: Matches model type to data structure correctly. Risk Assessment: Identifies obvious risks (e.g., "it might be wrong").

clos.description: Design technical solutions that address specific problems using technology.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Interactive Lectures: Machine Learning, Generative AI, Microsoft Foundry, Text Analysis Concepts, AI Speech
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Technical Design Document (TDD): A report detailing data sources, feature engineering plans, model selection rationale, Generative AI Prompt Battle, Text Analysis Entity Linking.

clos.description: Implement, deploy, and evaluate a machine learning model in a production-ready environment
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Lab Demonstrations: Step-by-step guides on using tools like Microsoft Foundry, Cloud ML platforms (Google Colab, Hugging Face)
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: End-to-end Development Pipeline & GitHub/Google Colab/Hugging Face/ Microsoft Foundry: Assessment of code quality, modularity, and documentation, development pipeline DEV/UAT/PROD. Performance Report: A technical evaluation of the model's performance on unseen data and its deployment latency.

clos.description: Present technical findings and project reports to stakeholders clearly.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Mock Presentations: Practice sessions with peer feedback on delivery, body language, and clarity of complex concepts. Ethics Retrospective: Provides the raw material and critical thinking needed to write a high-level ethical analysis.
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Final Presentation: A formal presentation (demo) to a "panel of stakeholders" focusing on business impact. Reflective Report: A comprehensive project report including ethical considerations and lessons learned.

weeks.teachingMethodsRaw: Case Study Analysis: the "Ethical Tribunal" (Role Play)
weeks.activeLearningRaw: Divide class into "Developers" and "Ethics Committee." Present a controversial AI case (e.g., facial recognition for hiring). "Developers" must argue for the utility, while the "Committee" applies the 6 Microsoft Responsible AI principles to reject or modify the proposal.

weeks.lectureTopic: Topic 2: Get started with AI in Microsoft Foundry
weeks.teachingMethodsRaw: Interactive Lecture: Platform Familiarity - UI Scavenger Hunt (Gamification)
weeks.activeLearningRaw: To reduce cognitive load in later weeks, turn the interface walkthrough into a race. Give a checklist of obscure features in Microsoft Foundry (e.g., "Find the Quota Limit," "Locate the Deploy button"). First team to screenshot all locations wins.

weeks.lectureTopic: Topic 4: Get started with machine learning in Azure
weeks.teachingMethodsRaw: Direct instruction and conceptual scaffolding: introduces the end-to-end ML lifecycle by mapping abstract steps—like data preparation, compute selection, and model training—to a high-stakes, real-world research problem
weeks.activeLearningRaw: Students engage in self-paced activities by reviewing the Microsoft Learn units to understand how to define a problem and structure a data pipeline.

weeks.lectureTopic: Topic 5: Introduction to generative AI and agents
weeks.teachingMethodsRaw: Interactive Lecture: The "Hallucination Hunt" LLM Limitations.
weeks.activeLearningRaw: Workflow Redesign: Students construct the "To-Be" (future) workflow incorporating the ML model's output.

weeks.activeLearningRaw: Students engage in self-paced activities by navigating the Microsoft Learn reading units to map out how computers process language

weeks.lectureTopic: Topic 10: Get started with speech in Microsoft Foundry

weeks.teachingMethodsRaw: Direct instruction and visual scaffolding: introduces how machines "see" by demonstrating everyday applications like smartphone facial recognition, automatic photo categorization

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged Examinations N/A Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
